headline: New weapon against brain-eating amoeba discovered

body:
UC San Diego researchers have discovered a marine-derived molecule that kills Naegleria fowleri faster and more selectively than existing treatments. The brain-eating amoeba ranks among the world's most lethal infections, making this breakthrough a significant step forward in combating a parasite with few effective defenses.

The discovery emerged from marine research, suggesting that ocean-derived compounds may hold untapped potential against some of medicine's most stubborn adversaries. By targeting the parasite with greater speed and precision, this new molecule could transform treatment options for an infection that has long posed a formidable challenge to medical science.

While details remain limited, the finding represents genuine progress in addressing a rare but devastating disease—one where faster, more effective interventions could mean the difference between recovery and tragedy.
quick_facts: UC San Diego researchers identified breakthrough treatment
Marine-derived molecule kills the amoeba faster
More selective action against the parasite
Naegleria fowleri among world's most lethal infections
